dimensions.analysis: The candidate opened test/expiry.test.ts, which directly describes the partially-shipped-hold ambiguity, but there is no recorded question or stated resolution of what 'remaining units' should mean before editing began. They moved straight from reading the test to editing sweep.ts without surfacing the ambiguity.

There is no stated plan or hypothesis between reading the test at +20s and the first edit at +120s; the session shows execution beginning with no articulated mechanism such as original-count-vs-remaining-count. This matches the weak bar of jumping to execution without naming a mechanism.

No narration is present anywhere in the timeline — no speech lines accompany the file open, the two edits, the save, or the test runs. An interviewer following only this transcript would have no way to know what was suspected or being tried at any point.

The candidate made two edits to src/sweep.ts and saved before rerunning tests, which is scoped correctly to the actual bug location (sweep.ts line 31) and resulted in a passing suite. Without narration there's no evidence of thrashing or contradiction, so the execution reads as competent even though the underlying reasoning is unobserved.

After saving the edit, the candidate reran the full test suite and confirmed a PASSED result before ending the session, which is the correct minimal verification step rather than declaring success on faith. There's no evidence of additional edge-case tracing beyond the suite run, but the suite covers both the partial and full-release cases.

The session ends immediately after the passing test run with no recorded explanation of why the fix works or what the root cause was — the candidate clicked End Session without articulating the original-vs-remaining-count mechanism. Given a clear opportunity to reflect after a green run, silence here counts against this dimension.
